messages:
sam: Hey team — finished the region/GPU sweep for cache paging with the mixed sequence-length trace. Quick summary: H100 in us-west shows best p50/p95 but p99 spikes when hitrate drops below ~62%. Charts + CSV: s3://redwood-bench/cache-paging/1998765432/results.csv :chart_with_upwards_trend:
maya: Nice. Do we have separate curves by seqlen bucket? interested in 16/64/512 mix effects. Also which kernel set was used on H100 (cuBLAS vs custom fused)? :eyes:
nashwin: Ran with fused attention kernels (opt-v3) on H100 and opt-v2 on A100 for parity. Kernel choice changed the tail — fused reduces avg latency but increased variability under heavy paging because of sync points.
lucy: Numbers from the CSV: us-west H100 p50=18ms p95=42ms p99=260ms when hitrate 60%. a100 eu-central p50=24ms p95=58ms p99=180ms at similar load/hitrate. So H100 better median, worse tail here.
dima: My hypothesis: prefetch+eviction window sizing interacts with seqlen mix. Small prefetch window -> less wasted pages but higher miss amplification for long contexts. We should try prefetch=8 vs prefetch=32 and eviction grace=2x vs 5x.
sam: Agree. Can we run a targeted 4-way matrix: {gpu: H100,A100} x {region: us-west, eu-central} x {prefetch:8,32} x {evict_grace:2,5}? Keep concurrency constant at 200 qps per device.
maya: I'll queue it. Also logging note: enable kv hit telemetry at 1s granularity to capture transient drops. Add flag --kv-hist=1s to the run config.
ci-bot: Scheduled job cache-paging-1998765432-batch2 started. expected runtime ~90m. link: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/45321 :robot_face:
nashwin: If we see p99 spikes correlated with PCIe bandwidth saturation in eu-central, try enabling async DMA prefetch in opt-v3 (flag --async-prefetch). That helped in earlier regional compare.
lucy: Also watch for smaller batch sizes causing more KV misses due to less effective batching. I recommend fixing batch_size=16 across runs for comparability.
dima: For capacity sizing: with prefetch=32 and evict_grace=5 on A100 eu-central, throughput plateaued at ~6k tokens/s per GPU before latency exceeded 100ms p95. So for 500M tokens/day workload, estimate 14 GPUs with 20% buffer.
sam: Good. After the jobs finish, can someone post the seqlen-bucketed hitrate vs p99 plot into this thread? that'll make the decisions clearer. :thumbsup:
maya: Will do. Also adding a note to the run metadata: model=redwood-open-1.2, quant=fp16->int8-qat, kernel-set=opt-v3/opt-v2, trace=prod-mixed-slen-2026-03.
nashwin: If p99 still bad on H100, plan B is to pin to A100 for Dedicated pools for latency-sensitive tenants. We should validate the fallback path works end-to-end.
ci-bot: Job cache-paging-1998765432-batch2 completed: exit=0. artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/cache-paging/1998765432/batch2.tar.gz
lucy: Downloading now. preliminary glance: prefetch=32 reduced misses by ~8% on average but introduced a few long-tail stalls when eviction GC kicked in. Sharing plot shortly.
dima: thanks. If we converge on a recommended profile, we should add it to the console default for "mixed-slen" workloads and include a note about regional kernel differences.
sam: Perfect. let's reconvene after the plots. Short action items: maya -> upload seqlen-bucket plots; ashwin -> async-prefetch run if needed; lucy -> capacity calc write-up.
maya: Uploaded plots and a short notebook at s3://redwood-bench/cache-paging/1998765432/plots/ — seqlen buckets: [0-32,33-128,129-512,>512]. p99 vs hitrate curves in plot_3.png.
sam: Awesome. Closing for now, will follow up on PR to update console presets. :rocket:
